evidence.claim: Built about 1860, it uses the Town lattice truss design developed by Ithiel Town.
evidence.quote: It is a Town lattice truss bridge following a design of Ithiel Town, built about 1860.

evidence.claim: In 1965, an engineering survey documented it as one of Delaware's last three surviving covered bridges.
evidence.quote: In 1965, when it was documented in the Historic American Engineering Record survey, it was one of the last three surviving covered bridges in the state of Delaware.

evidence.claim: The bridge entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

evidence.claim: Traffic has repeatedly damaged the structure: oversized trucks struck it in 2011 and 2014 after drivers ignored the signs, and a snowplow crashed in 2017.
evidence.quote: In 2014 and 2011, oversized trucks caused damage to the bridge after ignoring signage and attempting to cross, and in 2017 a snow plow crash caused additional damage.

evidence.claim: High water and debris during Hurricane Ida damaged the covered span in 2021, prompting another temporary repair closure.
evidence.quote: In 2021, it was closed for temporary repairs after debris and high creek levels due to Hurricane Ida caused damage to the covered portion of the span.

evidence.claim: Steam power links the Marshall family's mills with the cars preserved at Auburn Valley State Park.
evidence.quote: T. Clarence Marshall, the youngest son of Israel Marshall and the father of Thomas Marshall, was fascinated by the steam power that operated the family's mills.

evidence.claim: T. Clarence Marshall became a Stanley dealer and collected steam automobiles; the collection opened to the public in the 1970s.
evidence.quote: He became a licensed dealer for Stanley Motor Carriage Company and began acquiring a personal collection of steam automobiles. The collection was first opened to the public in the 1970s.

evidence.claim: Volunteers maintain the vehicles in working order in the Auburn Heights carriage house.
evidence.quote: The collection is housed in the Auburn Heights carriage house, where a team of volunteers maintains the vehicles so that they remain fully operational.

evidence.claim: The collection includes 15 Stanley cars and a one-eighth-size steam locomotive that runs on tracks encircling the estate.
evidence.quote: Included in the collection are 15 Stanley cars and several steam and electric cars from other manufacturers. The Museum's collection also includes a 1/8-size steam locomotive that runs on tracks around the estate called the Auburn Valley Railroad.

evidence.claim: Tom Marshall donated the collection in 2008; the nonprofit Friends of Auburn Heights Preserve owns it and works with the state.
evidence.quote: Following its donation in 2008 by Tom Marshall, the collection is owned by the nonprofit Friends of Auburn Heights Preserve which operates the park in partnership with the state.

evidence.claim: Above the mills and Yorklyn stands the Victorian mansion Israel Marshall built in 1897.

evidence.claim: Above the mills and Yorklyn stands the Victorian mansion
evidence.quote: The home was built in a Victorian style, and is situated on a large hill so that it overlooks the mill complex, and the town of Yorklyn, below.

evidence.quote: It was destroyed by flooding from Tropical Storm Henri in 2003. The bridge was rebuilt by the Delaware Department of Transportation in 2007–8 with design modifications to make it more flood-resistant.
